predictions.claim: The US is headed toward a ban on open-source/open-weight AI models, justified by 'guardrail' and bio/cyber-threat rhetoric being seeded now.
predictions.speaker: David Sacks

predictions.claim: If the US bans open models, the rest of the world will end up running on Chinese open-weight models.
predictions.speaker: Bill Gurley

predictions.claim: Cheaper, closer-to-bare-metal training stacks (an order-of-magnitude speedup) will shift training from $10B runs to $10M runs, spawning multiple open-source training stacks.
predictions.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

predictions.claim: The AI market will monopolize into a duopoly, with Anthropic potentially pulling away — 10x vs 3x growth yields ~90% share within two years if sustained.
predictions.speaker: David Sacks
predictions.notes: Sacks flags compute and competitive constraints may break the growth rate.

predictions.claim: The majority of cab and truck drivers (of ~20M in the US) will lose their jobs to self-driving within the next decade or two.
predictions.speaker: Jason Calacanis
predictions.notes: Gurley counters that human drivers may persist for ~50% of rides and total numbers could stay flat or grow.

predictions.claim: AI will lead to net job gains, not job loss, with a Cambrian explosion of bespoke software and new company creation; unemployment stays near record lows.
predictions.speaker: David Sacks

predictions.claim: Token efficiency will be the dominant enterprise AI theme over the next year as spend ramps faster than expected, tempering growth.
predictions.speaker: David Sacks

predictions.claim: AI-driven productivity will make goods and services cheaper through competition rather than producing obscene profits or 70% operating margins.
predictions.speaker: Bill Gurley
predictions.notes: Caveats that healthcare and regulated industries may not see the same price declines.
